Fifteen formats, one method: how Bobine learned to edit

A video editor that lives in the browser, keeps your footage on your phone, and cuts to the beat of your own music.

Bobine began as a favour to friends who publish every day and spend their nights on the timeline. The rule from the first sketch: the footage never leaves the device, and the result has to look like a professional cut.

Each format got its own editing agent with its own brief: a vlog is not a product launch, a podcast clip is not a paper collage. The agent plans, cuts, reviews its own work and repairs what is wrong.

To show it, I cut thirteen one minute edits from real footage, each in both aspect ratios, and a motion design that explains the whole thing in fifty seconds. They are all in the gallery here, and on the landing page.
